title: Eagle Eye
problem: This box designs the eagle-eye skill on itself. The skill must decide who builds a box and who reads it back. It must also decide how honest an edge claims to be, where the file lives, and what the page shows. The answers change each other. A page that a person edits needs a round trip, and a round trip needs a stable file format.
who: The author of the skill, and every agent and reader who builds a box with it.
when: Before the skill shipped, and the author settled it on 2026-08-23.

dims.problem: A morphological box needs somebody to build it and somebody to read a change back. The agent could do both, or hand a page to a person and never see it again. This row decides whether a box is a one-way artifact the agent produces, or a document a person edits and returns for the agent to re-argue.
dims.name: Who drives it

opts.label: The agent’s reasoning method: it builds the box in chat; the page is optional
A generator: the agent emits the page, you do the thinking
Both, round-tripped: the agent builds, you override and export, it re-argues
No tool — keep asking one question at a time

dims.problem: A skill only helps if it starts at the right moment. Too eager and it builds a grid for two unrelated choices. Too shy and a tangled discussion never gets one. This row decides what wakes the skill: an explicit request, a coupling the agent notices, a host flow that calls it, or all three.
dims.name: When it fires

opts.label: By name only: /eagle-eye
On the coupling smell alone: 3+ decisions where one pick changes another
As a stage inside another host flow
Signal + host stages, with the name as fallback

dims.problem: An edge colours the grid, so a reader treats it as a fact. Some edges come from a measurement, some from a named document, and some from the author's own reasoning. This row decides whether the page shows that difference, and how much a weak edge must admit before it may colour anything.
dims.name: Edge honesty

opts.label: Evidence required: no edge without a citation
Reasoning is enough: a one-line why
Tiered and labelled: measured / sourced / argued
Just the edge, no why at all

dims.problem: After a reader changes an option, the page can report a verdict and stop, or it can point at what the reader has not looked at. A verdict alone closes the question. This row decides whether the panel also names the untouched row, the weakest edge, and the strawman that nothing ruled out.
dims.name: What the panel says

opts.label: The verdict only: consistent / incomplete / does not hold
The six moves: untouched row, weakest edge, load-bearing option, free row, survived strawman, cogency test

dims.problem: People remember a system better when they predict its behaviour before they see it. A page can force that, offer it, or skip it. Forcing it makes a quick lookup slow. This row decides whether prediction exists at all, and whether the reader opts in.
dims.name: Coach layer

opts.label: None
Opt-in: predict before reveal
Always on: every override is a quiz

dims.problem: Every edge is a reason, and a reason can be wrong in eight known ways. Checking all of them is thorough and slow. Checking none ships colour the reader cannot trust. This row decides which edges are audited before the box is rendered.
dims.name: Edge audit

opts.label: None
The eight weakness patterns, on argued edges
On every edge, every tier

dims.problem: A skill file sits either in the user's own directory or inside one repository. In the user's directory it works everywhere and travels with the person. In a repository it ships to a team and is reviewed like code. This row picks where the skill is installed.
dims.name: Where it lives

opts.label: User-level: the user's own skills directory
This repo: a skills directory, beside the project's other skills
Developed here, promoted later

dims.problem: A box file always exists during the session, because the round trip and --sel both read it. This row decides where it is written, and so whether the project keeps it afterwards. A file in the repository lets a later session re-argue the same decisions. It also becomes one more document to keep true, and it asks every later reader to learn a grid to read one choice.
dims.name: Where a box is written

opts.label: Disposable: one file in scratch, no trace in the repository
Kept: one file per coupled decision, in the project's records, on request

dims.problem: The page could be written by the model each time, produced by a fixed renderer from a data file, or served by a full command-line tool. A page re-authored each time drifts the export format that the round trip depends on. This row decides how much machinery the skill carries.
dims.name: How it is built

opts.label: Prompt-only: the agent hand-writes the page from a template
Skill + zero-dep renderer: box file in, page out
A proper command-line tool: validate, render, diff

dims.problem: The rendered box has to reach the reader somehow: a local file they open, a hosted page with a link, or nothing beyond the chat. Hosting needs a tool that is not always available. This row decides the delivery, and what happens when the preferred one is missing.
dims.name: Where the page goes

opts.label: A local HTML file, opened in the browser; a hosted page when available
Hosted page only
No page: the markdown table is the whole tool

dims.problem: The box is data before it is a page, and something has to hold it. JSON is strict and every tool reads it. YAML is easier to write by hand and easier to get wrong. Embedding it in the page removes the separate file, and the round trip with it. This row picks the format.
dims.name: Box file format

opts.label: JSON
YAML
Embedded in the page, as the earlier artifact does

dims.problem: Not every set of decisions deserves a rendered page. Three coupled choices fit in a table in the chat. Fifteen need splitting into clusters. This row decides what picks the output: the number of rows, a flag the user passes, or the full treatment every time.
dims.name: Depth control

opts.label: By row count: 2–3 rows a chat table, 4+ a page, 15+ split
A flag the user passes
Always the full page, no tuning

dims.problem: The command name is what the user types and what the agent recognises. It has to be memorable, unlikely to collide with another command, and suggestive of what the tool does. This row picks between the metaphor, the technical term, and the short generic word.
dims.name: Name

opts.label: /eagle-eye
/morph
/box

driver-both.why: Chosen. The restore code in the earlier artifact already hints at the loop; the page is the surface you think on, the export is what the agent reads back.
rel: A round trip needs an export format both sides agree on; a page re-authored by hand each time drifts it.
The round trip reads the separate box file with JSON.parse. A YAML file fails that parse, and Embedded in page has no separate file.
notes: The export→agent half is the artifact’s own design; the agent→file half is new and untested.

driver-method.why: The agent builds the box in conversation and checks its own recommendation against it; the page is optional.
rel: Predict-before-reveal withholds a verdict the page computes; in chat the agent would have to withhold its own sentence.

driver-gen.why: The agent emits the page; the thinking is yours.
rel: The audit is the agent checking edges it drew; a generator that does no reasoning has nothing to audit.

driver-none.why: Strawman: no tool. One question at a time, as today.
rel: No tool writes no file, in scratch or anywhere else.
No tool writes no file, so nothing reaches the project's records.
notes: The honest comparison: you said a box resolves a question-at-a-time session as fast as you can read it. That is the claim this strawman tests.

trig-full.why: Chosen. The smell is the trigger; the hosts are where it shows up; the name is for when you see the coupling first.
rel: A skill that fires itself must size its own output, or a three-row question gets a full page.

trig-signal.why: Fires on the coupling smell only.
rel: Nobody is there to pass a flag when the skill fires on its own.

trig-hosts.why: A stage inside another host flow.
rel: The hosts are global plugins; a repo-level skill makes a global flow behave differently per repo.

notes: No edges: a human-pulled trigger constrains nothing else. Zero false fires, zero reach.

edge-tiered.why: Chosen. Every edge says what it rests on; the verdict says what tier it rests on.
notes: This option and Argued edges required each other. The cycle finding named the pair as one decision drawn twice.
The box now keeps one direction. The audit needs a tier to select on. A tier needs no audit.

rel: Evidence required keeps only cited edges. This box has three, so most moves have almost nothing to read.
notes: Count the sourced edges in this box: that is what an evidence-only grid of the same decision looks like.

rel: The weakest-edge move ranks by tier; with one tier there is no weakest.
The audit targets argued edges; untiered, it runs on all of them or none.

edge-bare.why: Strawman: the edge exists, nobody says why.
rel: The cogency test asks whether the whys could all be true; there are none.

moves-six.why: Chosen. A box that returns only consistent / does not hold is a checker; one that returns the thing you haven’t looked at is a thinking tool.
rel: The weakest-edge move needs a tier to rank by.
notes: The panel computes seven findings now. The chain finding joined the six after this box was drawn. The option keeps its name, because the name records what the decision was.

moves-verdict.why: Strawman: the verdict and nothing else — the earlier artifact as it stands.
notes: This is the artifact you already have. If it survives the box, the six moves are decoration.

coach-optin.why: Chosen. Predict which rows an override breaks, then reveal. Retrieval practice, borrowed from the tutoring skill.
notes: Try it: the toggle above. Then decide whether it is the strongest move or a quiz nobody asked for.
The chain finding once named a relation here, through Skill + renderer. That edge is now in suspected, so the path is gone.

coach-always.why: Strawman: every override is a quiz.

audit-argued.why: Chosen. The TDE coach’s eight weakness patterns, run on argued edges only.
rel: The audit needs to know which edges are argued.

notes: A plausible wrong edge then looks identical to a right one — the failure the tiers were meant to make visible.
Auditing a measured edge against “is it vague?” is re-running the measurement in prose. Cost, no catch.

home-user.why: Chosen. A thinking tool is yours, not the project’s; and you plan to share it from your own skill repo.

home-repo.why: Versioned beside the project's other skills; only this repo gets it.
rel: A committed command that invokes a plugin only one machine has is the trap; a repo skill that hooks global flows is its mirror.

notes: Two copies to keep in step; the promotion is a chore nobody schedules.

persist-scratch.why: Chosen. The box is the working surface for one conversation. The decision it produces belongs in the project's records, not the grid that found it.
notes: Disposable is not ephemeral. The file exists for the whole session, because --sel and the round trip both read it.
A committed box asks every later reader to learn a grid to read one choice.

persist-decision.why: One file per coupled decision, written where the project keeps its records. The user asks for this; it is never the default.

build-renderer.why: Chosen. The agent thinks and writes data; a zero-dep script renders, deterministically. Grid logic lives in one place.
rel: A renderer reads a file; data embedded in the page is the artifact’s shape, not a renderer’s input.
the #186 artifact: DIMS/REL are literals inside the page

build-prompt.why: The agent hand-writes the page each time.
rel: Predict-then-reveal is page state, re-implemented per page.
The export format drifts with every re-authoring.
notes: The grid logic would be re-derived by a model each time; the bugs would be quiet.

build-tool.why: A command-line tool with validate / render / diff / moves.
notes: A product, not a skill. Nothing here rules it out — that is worth noticing. It is “too early”, which is a preference, not an edge.

page-local.why: Chosen. Works anywhere Node runs; a hosted page when one is there.

page-artifact.why: Publish as a hosted page only.
rel: A portable, shareable skill cannot assume a hosting service is reachable.

page-chat.why: Strawman: no page. The markdown table is the tool.
rel: No export to round-trip; the table is edited by hand or not at all.
notes: For 2–3 rows this is already what depth-by-rows does. The strawman asks: why not always?

data-json.why: Chosen. Node parses it with nothing installed.

rel: Node has no built-in YAML parser; zero-dep means JSON.
Node.js: JSON.parse is global; no yaml module in core

data-embedded.why: Data inside the page, as the artifact does today.

depth-rows.why: Chosen. Depth follows the row count, not a flag.

depth-always.why: Strawman: no tuning at all; every box is the full page.
notes: You asked for tuning so it “doesn’t go too deep on easy decisions”. Nothing structural enforces that — watch whether this strawman survives.

wrong: driver-both req persist-decision — the round trip needs a file, and both cells of that row write one. The edge named the wrong requirement. It is now a requirement on the file format, not on where the file lives. Retired 2026-08-30 when the row changed to scratch or kept.

weakly connected: driver-gen conf moves-six — the box places the six moves on the page's panel, and a generator still emits the page; nothing in the box says that page lacks the panel. Why: "The moves are the panel reasoning about the set; a pure generator draws the grid and stops."

insufficient: coach-optin req build-renderer — the why argues only against Prompt-only, yet the requirement also rules out Full command-line tool, which nothing else rules out. Why: "Withhold-then-reveal is page state; prompt-only re-implements it on every page."

biased: coach-always conf depth-rows — the entry above already rejects this reason as a preference, not a constraint; By row count still gives a page at four rows or more, where the quiz runs. Why: "A three-row chat table with a withheld verdict is a quiz nobody asked for."

weakly connected: persist-scratch req data-json — where the file is written does not pick its format; the renderer does, and Skill + renderer already rules out YAML and Embedded in page with sourced edges. Why: "A file needs a format the renderer reads with nothing installed."

weakly connected: persist-decision req data-json — where the file is written does not pick its format; the renderer does, and Skill + renderer already rules out YAML and Embedded in page with sourced edges. Why: "A file needs a format the renderer reads with nothing installed."

weakly connected: data-embedded conf persist-scratch — the page itself can be the one file in scratch; the real loss is the round trip, which the data row problem names and which belongs to another row. Why: "The page is the file, so regenerating the page overwrites the data."

weakly connected: data-embedded conf persist-decision — a project can keep the page as its one file, so the missing separate record does not stop a kept box; the real loss is the round trip. Why: "The page is the file, so a kept box has no separate record to keep."

presets.title: Start
presets.text: No option is changed. Read the findings. Then open row 04 to see each option and its effect.
presets.reframe: The problem is still the whole design, and the box tests none of it until you change an option.

presets.title: Change one option
presets.text: Open row 09 and pick “Prompt-only”. Two other rows become amber. Then open the Sheet view and move the pointer over the options.
presets.reframe: The problem narrows to one question: what does a skill without a page cost the reader?

presets.title: Coach
presets.text: Set Coach to on. Change row 07 to “This repo”. The index shows no colours. Click the rows you think are affected. Then click Reveal.
presets.reframe: The problem becomes how a reader learns the grid, not which option the grid picks.

presets.title: Strawmen
presets.text: Change row 01 to “No tool”. Three edges rule it out. Reset. Change row 04 to “Verdict only”. No row becomes amber: no option in the design requires the six moves.
presets.reframe: The problem becomes whether anything in the box rules the weak answers out.
